title: Two-bucket gravity water filter
summary: Make a two-bucket gravity filter from food-grade buckets and a salvaged filter cartridge (ceramic or hollow-fibre is best, a fridge or under-sink carbon block is second best). It clears mud and improves taste, but most salvaged filters do not reliably remove germs. Always boil or disinfect the filtered water before drinking.

materials.item: Two food-grade buckets with lids, 10–20 L
Filter element: ceramic candle or hollow-fibre filter best; fridge, pitcher or under-sink carbon cartridge second best
Rubber, silicone or foam gaskets and washers to seal the filter through the bucket, food-safe where they touch filtered water
Food-safe tap or valve for the lower (clean-water) bucket
Food-grade tubing and fittings to adapt a fridge or under-sink cartridge
Clean cloth for a pre-filter (cotton sheet, T-shirt), washed and boiled first
Activated carbon, if using a layered filter
Plain unscented household bleach (5–6%) for disinfecting the output
Washed sand and gravel, for the layered variant

steps.text: Get two food-grade buckets (marked HDPE, #2 or food-safe). Wash them with soap, then rinse with water holding a capful of bleach per bucket. Mark one DIRTY and one CLEAN.
steps.warn: Never use buckets that held paint, solvent, oil, pesticide or pool chemicals. Traces stay in the plastic.

steps.text: Pick the filter. Ceramic candles and hollow-fibre filters (0.1–0.2 micron) stop bacteria and parasites. Carbon blocks from fridges and under-sink units improve taste and some chemicals but cannot be trusted against germs. Prefer sealed spares; used cartridges may be growing bacteria. A filter that froze wet may be broken inside with no sign: check it first ([Check a found or frozen water filter](#guides/test_water_filter)).

Drill a hole in the bottom centre of the DIRTY bucket to fit the filter's outlet stem, and a matching hole in the CLEAN bucket's lid. For a fridge or under-sink cartridge, fit a short tube from its outlet through the hole.
Fit the filter with a gasket on each side of the bucket wall and tighten. Pour in water and check for drips around the seal.
steps.warn: Any leak around the filter lets dirty water bypass it. Fix every drip before you trust the output.

steps.text: Drill a hole about 5 cm above the bottom of the CLEAN bucket and fit the tap with gaskets on both sides.
New carbon cartridges shed black dust: run 10–20 L through and throw it away. Soak ceramic candles in clean water for 15 minutes first.
Let muddy water settle in another container for 1–12 hours, pour off the clear part through the cloth, then pour it into the DIRTY bucket. Mud clogs filters fast.

Disinfect what comes out: bring to a rolling boil for 1 minute (at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m, Health Canada BWA), or add 2 drops of plain 5–6% bleach per litre (4 if still cloudy), stir and wait 30 minutes (below 10 °C, double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours: HealthLinkBC 49b). It should smell faintly of chlorine, but noses differ (Health Canada chlorine TD). A pool or spa test kit that reads free chlorine is a better check: after the wait, aim for at least 0.5 mg/L free chlorine (WEDC Mobile Note 7, quoting WHO). If it reads lower, or you smell nothing, add the same dose again and wait 15 minutes more (EPA water).
steps.warn: Filtered water is NOT safe yet. Viruses pass every filter here, and carbon cartridges let bacteria through.

steps.text: Keep the CLEAN side clean: never dip cups into it, never let dirty water or hands touch the tap or the lower bucket.

When flow slows, scrub ceramic candles with a clean pad under clean water; backflush hollow-fibre filters as their maker intended. Replace carbon cartridges at the capacity or date on their label, or sooner if flow drops: GE rates its MWF fridge cartridge at 170 or 300 US gal (about 640 or 1,140 L) or 6 months, whichever comes first (GE). Change it too when the taste or smell comes back (UGA).

notes:
## What it removes
| Problem | Ceramic / hollow-fibre | Carbon block cartridge | Sand + charcoal layers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mud, cloudiness | Yes | Yes | Mostly |
| Parasites (Giardia, Cryptosporidium) | Yes | Some blocks, not reliably | Partly |
| Bacteria | Mostly | No | Partly |
| Viruses | No | No | No |
| Taste, smell, chlorine, some pesticides | No (unless it has carbon) | Yes, until used up | Some |
| Salt, nitrate, fluoride, most dissolved metals | No | No | No |
| Fuel or industrial chemicals | No | Partly; don't trust it | No |

**Nothing here makes water safe on its own. Always boil or disinfect afterwards.** Filtering first makes boiling and bleach work better, because germs hide in mud.

## Flow you can expect
These are the sources' own figures in their own test set-ups, not measured at your bucket.
- Ceramic candle filter: CAWST gives 0.1–1 L an hour, fastest when the top bucket is full and slowing as the pores clog. More than one candle raises the flow (CAWST ceramic).
- Hollow-fibre gravity filter: Katadyn rates its BeFree gravity bag at up to 2 L a minute (Katadyn BeFree manual).
- Fridge or under-sink carbon block: built for mains pressure. GE lists a service flow of 0.5 US gal (1.9 L) a minute for its MWF fridge cartridge, on water supplied at 2.8–8.2 bar (GE); a bucket gives far less push, so expect much less (no maker figure).
- Reverse-osmosis membranes need real pressure: Pentair's under-sink unit wants 2.75–6.9 bar (Pentair RO-2550). A bucket 0.4 m high gives about 0.04 bar. They won't work here.

## Layered sand and charcoal variant
From the top of the DIRTY bucket down: cloth, 30–40 cm of fine washed sand, 10 cm of activated carbon (or crushed charcoal from a wood fire, which is weaker) wrapped in cloth, 5 cm of fine gravel, 5 cm of coarse gravel, then the outlet. Treat it as a mud strainer, not a germ filter. Sand only grows the living layer that eats germs when about 5 cm (2 in) of water stands on the sand, held there by a raised outlet, and it is used at least every 1–2 days; even then the layer takes up to 30 days to form, and without it sand removes only about 30–70 % of germs (CAWST manual). A bucket with its outlet at the bottom drains the water down below the sand, which CAWST says dries the filter out (CAWST manual). For a filter built to do it, see [Build a biosand filter](#guides/build_biosand_filter). Still boil or disinfect.

## Bleach dose
Plain bleach only: no scent, no "splash-less" or cleaning additives. 5–6% bleach: 2 drops per litre, 8 drops per 4 L. 8.25% bleach: about 1.5 drops per litre, 6 drops per 4 L (CDC make water safe, EPA water). Wait 30 minutes. Below 10 °C (50 °F), double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours, covered (HealthLinkBC 49b). Bleach loses strength with age and heat. Use bleach that is fresh or has been kept at room temperature for under a year (EPA water), and keep it cool, dry and out of the sun (EPA bleach label). Clorox says bleach over a year old is too weak to disinfect (Clorox date). Don't guess a stronger dose for old bleach: use a fresh bottle, or test the water. A pool or spa test kit that reads free chlorine (a DPD kit, not an OTO kit) is a better check than smell (San Bernardino pool kit, WHO chlorine test). Aim for at least 0.5 mg/L after the wait if the pH is below 8 (WEDC Mobile Note 7, quoting WHO; MSF cholera). Above pH 8, see [Test water with found kits](#guides/test_water). If it reads lower, repeat the dose (EPA water, EPA bleach label).

## Other ways to disinfect
- Boiling: a rolling boil for 1 minute, at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m (Health Canada BWA). Boiling doesn't remove nitrate and can raise it (Health Canada BWA), so well water that may hold nitrate needs a test or another source before it goes into a baby's formula (AHS nitrate).
- Sunlight (SODIS): clear plastic bottles, 6 hours of sun or 2 days of cloud, and only in strong sun: in a Canadian winter boil or chlorinate instead. See [Solar disinfection](#guides/skill_solar_disinfection).

## Frost
A filter that froze wet may be broken with nothing to show for it. Katadyn says a frozen hollow-fibre membrane can let germs through, and Sawyer says there's no sure way to tell, so it advises replacing a filter you think froze (Katadyn BeFree manual, Sawyer FAQ). Berkey says never let its wet elements freeze, as they can crack or break (Berkey elements), and CAWST warns that cracks too fine to see let germs through a ceramic candle (CAWST ceramic). Keep the filter in a heated room. Treat one that froze as broken unless it passes a check: [Check a found or frozen water filter](#guides/test_water_filter).

## Where to find cartridges
Fridges with water dispensers, under-sink and reverse-osmosis units, water coolers, ice machines, pitchers, coffee machines, and well systems (sediment cartridges). Camping shops and outdoor gear stores stock ceramic and hollow-fibre filters.

**Don't use carbon from air purifiers or cooker hoods.** It isn't food-grade and may be treated with chemicals.

## If you lack a part
- No tap: siphon from the CLEAN bucket with clean tubing.
- No cartridge: use the layered sand and charcoal variant, and boil.
- No food-grade bucket: stainless steel pots or clean drinks containers work.
